title: The package scope names the architectural tier
subject: main
summary: Scope every workspace package by its tier: `@configs/*` · `@libs/*` · `@modules/*` · `@features/*` · `@apps/*`. Apps get a scope even though nothing imports the

adr.context: Every workspace package was scoped `@prowd/*` — one product scope covering configs, libraries, seed slices and apps alike. At an import site a [[library]], a [[seed slice]] and an [[product slice]] were indistinguishable, so the import boundaries this repo is built on were invisible in the code that violates them, and no boundary rule could be written against the specifier itself.
adr.decision: Scope every workspace package by its tier: `@configs/*` · `@libs/*` · `@modules/*` · `@features/*` · `@apps/*`. Apps get a scope even though nothing imports them, because the scope namespace is the vocabulary the boundary rules are written in — `nothing imports an app` is only statable if an app is nameable.
consequences: A violation is readable at the call site: `@modules/a` importing `@modules/b` is wrong on sight, without knowing the codebase.
Every boundary rule becomes a scope-to-scope lint pattern — no path globs, no resolver knowledge. AC44's linter gets cheap.
Promoting an [[product slice|product slice]] to a [[seed slice]] rewrites every import of it. That is intended: crossing a tier is a deliberate act and should be visible in the diff.
A seed slice shipped to another product stops carrying this product's name.

**Constraint:** non-registry scopes work only because the seed is distributed by cloning the repo. If seed seed slices were ever published to a registry, `@modules` and `@libs` are not ownable npm scopes and this decision would have to be reversed.

Migration is a bijection (`@prowd/x` → `@<tier>/x`, tier fixed by the folder) touching ~337 import sites in ~277 files. It belongs in one commit of its own, applied by a script: the compiler catches every miss, but only a deterministic rewrite prevents two spellings of the same package.
Open: `team-cockpit/` sits outside the five tiers and has no scope assigned.
